rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: Quiet Storm history. Label mechanics. The personnel and format infrastructure behind the slow jam economy.

questions.question: The Quiet Storm late-night radio format was pioneered by DJ Melvin Lindsey at which Washington D.C. radio station?

metadata.fact: DJ Melvin Lindsey launched the Quiet Storm format at WHUR-FM (Howard University's radio station) in 1976 — the format spread nationally through the early 1980s and became the primary home for R&B slow jams through the 90s.
metadata.storyHook: A college radio station in D.C. invented the format that every R&B slow jam artist in this episode owes their career to.

questions.question: Tyrese Gibson was discovered as a teenager after appearing in a nationally broadcast commercial for which soft drink brand?

metadata.fact: Tyrese Gibson was discovered at age 16 after appearing in a 1994 Coca-Cola commercial — singing 'Always Coca-Cola' while riding a city bus. The ad launched his career and led directly to his record deal.
metadata.storyHook: A fast food commercial launched one of the smoothest R&B careers of the late 90s. The slow jam pipeline ran through the golden arches.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Tyrese's breakthrough commercial was for Coca-Cola, not McDonald's. Sources: YouTube, theGrio, Mashed.

questions.question: Brian McKnight's brother Claude is a founding member of which celebrated Christian a cappella group?

metadata.fact: Claude McKnight co-founded Take 6 — the Grammy-winning Christian a cappella sextet — while his brother Brian McKnight pursued a secular R&B career, making the McKnight family one of the most musically accomplished in 90s gospel and R&B.
metadata.storyHook: Two brothers. Two lanes. Gospel and R&B split between them at birth.

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: Format founding history. Label archaeology. The infrastructure underneath the slow jam economy that only obsessives ever tracked.

questions.question: The Quiet Storm radio format takes its name from a 1975 Smokey Robinson album released on which Motown imprint?

metadata.fact: Smokey Robinson's Quiet Storm was released on Tamla — one of Motown's several imprint labels — in 1975. DJ Melvin Lindsey named his WHUR-FM late-night format after the album the following year, and the format has never left radio since.
metadata.storyHook: An album title became a radio format became an entire aesthetic that defined 20 years of R&B. It started on a Motown sub-label most people have never heard of.

questions.question: Next — the Minneapolis trio behind 'Too Close' — released their debut on which independent label distributed through Arista?

metadata.fact: Next released Rated Next on Divine Mill Records — an independent imprint distributed through Arista — giving the Minneapolis trio major label reach through an indie structure that preserved their creative control.
metadata.storyHook: Three guys from Minneapolis getting national distribution through a label most people needed Google to find.

questions.question: Smokey Robinson's 'Quiet Storm' album — which gave a radio format its name — was released in what year?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — YEAR SMOKEY'S QUIET STORM ALBUM DROPPED

metadata.fact: Smokey Robinson's Quiet Storm was released in 1975 on Tamla Records — DJ Melvin Lindsey named his WHUR-FM radio segment after it the following year, and the format spread nationally through the late 1970s and 1980s.
metadata.storyHook: A 1975 album nobody talks about anymore built the format that every artist in this episode depended on.
